review_candidates.company: BlueSky Utility - Powered by Nofar Energy
review_candidates.description: Senior Project Manager - Project Delivery Our Mission The Senior Project Manager - Project Delivery role centers around driving technical and commercial outcomes in pursuit of facility construction. We oversee the construction of projects, working with utilities who connect our projects to the grid, offtakers who purchase our power, and the lenders who finance them. You own the coordination between these parties, you report to the Director of Project Delivery, and you bring our projects online in fulfillment of our obligations, on schedule and within budget. You carry a portfolio of PV and battery storage projects, usually two or three at a time, from origination to Final Completion. What We Do As a Senior Project Manager, you'll work as part of a team of engineers, financial professionals, construction experts, and business managers to plan, design, finance, and construct PV Arrays and Battery Energy Storage Systems. Your mandate is facilitating collaboration across Nofar USA's functions and managing budgets and schedules throughout project development, preconstruction, construction, and commissioning. You drive those outcomes the whole way, and you hand the project over at Final Completion. You'll be at the center of our business workflows, inside and outside the company. You'll work with business development and finance on asset acquisitions, identifying risks and planning how to turn our growth strategy into reality. You'll lead RFPs to procure construction services and purchase critical equipment, and you'll carry those agreements through negotiation and administration. During EPCA turns, you consolidate comments and edits, lead the calls that close them, keep the exhibits and the exhibits tracker in order, and negotiate the statement of values with the counterparty. You'll manage interconnection agreements with the utility and the ISO, and you'll work with finance so procurement and construction information reaches our lenders in a form they can rely on. You'll be the subject matter expert of our execution process, keeping Nofar USA accountable to our PPA counterparties, lenders, and utilities, and keeping our vendors and construction partners accountable to us. Your job will evolve with the project lifecycle, but you can generally expect to: Coordinate with EPCs on engineering and construction progress, ensuring that they adhere to the project schedule. Oversee document submittals at key contract milestones. Report progress statistics to senior management during steering committee calls. Manage budgets, review and approve invoices, move critical project transactions, and work with Nofar USA controls so financial reporting is accurate Work with engineering and procurement to confirm critical equipment specifications, so the equipment can deliver the power we sold and is bankable Lead RFPs for construction services and negotiate price and commercial terms Consolidate EPCA comments and exhibits, lead the calls that close the comments, keep the exhibits tracker current, and negotiate the statement of values through to NTP Attend meetings with utility companies and manage utility and ISO interconnection agreements against the construction schedule Work with business development and finance to identify execution risks on acquisitions, and supply the procurement and construction information lenders need Report PPA milestones, track the schedule risk around those dates, and hold vendors and contractors to what they owe us Travel to projects and partners for up to 25% of your time, and work remotely the rest Reconcile the schedule, the cost, and the contract record so that at Final Completion the next team can take the project Requirements What We Value People who are driven to succeed, and who can work with minimal oversight Detail-oriented people. The tracker, the milestone report, and the budget are useful only when they are right Opinionated colleagues, willing to say how a project ought to be run People who are passionate about a career bringing power assets online People who are comfortable in a growth organization, where the way we work is still being shaped by the people doing the work What We Require Remote or Hybrid work, with up to 25% travel A minimum of three years delivering utility-scale solar or battery storage. Five years is preferred Required experience in preconstruction, managing budgets, and managing schedules Preferred experience with PPA milestone management, utility, and ISO interconnection agreements, EPCA negotiation and administration, and working with finance on lender reporting during procurement and construction We look for degrees in mathematics, statistics, engineering, the sciences, finance, and business. But if you believe you can do this job, we encourage you to apply Preference will be given to candidates in Fort Lauderdale, FL Benefits What We Offer A Lean Team Where Your Work Actually Matters We operate with a lean, highly capable team, which means there aren’t layers of people between you and the work that matters. You’ll have real ownership, direct access to decision-makers, and the opportunity to influence how we build and grow the business. If you want to be a meaningful voice rather than a small part of a very large machine, you’ll find that opportunity here. A Fast Pace and a High Bar We believe in being transparent about what it’s like to work here: we move quickly, the workload can be demanding, and our expectations are high. This is an environment for people who enjoy being challenged, solving problems, taking initiative, and figuring things out as we grow. In return, you’ll gain exposure, responsibility, and influence that can take years to earn in a more traditional organization. Who Thrives Here The people who do best at Blue Sky are proactive, resourceful, and comfortable taking ownership. They don’t wait to be told what to do next, and they’re willing to step outside the boundaries of a job description when the business needs it. They care about outcomes more than watching the clock, bring solutions instead of simply identifying problems, and genuinely enjoy the energy — and occasional ambiguity — that comes with building a growing company. If you’re a go-getter who wants room to run, you’ll fit in well here. Benefits That Invest In You We offer medical, dental, and vision insurance, short-term disability, life insurance, and a 401(k) with a generous 6% company match. Hybrid, With Purpose We believe there is real value in being together. Our hybrid model creates regular opportunities for in-person collaboration, faster decision-making, and stronger relationships while still providing flexibility outside of the office. What to Expect From Our Hiring Process We’re Choosy — On Purpose. We fiercely protect the culture we’ve built, and our hiring process reflects that. Skills and experience matter, but so does how you work, how you collaborate, and what you’ll add to the team. We want to get to know the person behind the résumé — and we want you to have plenty of opportunity to get to know us, too. Our Typical Hiring Process Looks Like This HR Screen → Hiring Manager Interview → Culture Assessment → Case Study, when applicable → Cross-Team Interview → CEO Meet & Greet → Offer Not every role requires a case study, but for certain positions we use one to better understand how you think, approach problems, and tackle the type of work you would actually be doing here. It Sounds Like a Lot. It Doesn’t Take a Lot of Time. We’re deliberate in our hiring decisions, but we’re also decisive. Our average turnaround from initial HR screen to offer is less than two weeks . We move quickly and respect that candidates have jobs, lives, and other opportunities in motion. You’ll Always Know Where You Stand. Clear communication is an important part of our candidate experience. We’ll be transparent about the process and expectations from the beginning, keep you informed as you move through each stage, and close the loop when a decision has been made. We believe every candidate deserves clarity and respect for the time they invest in getting to know us. We’re intentional about who joins our team because every person on a lean team has an outsized impact. When we make an offer, it’s because we’re genuinely excited about what you can bring to the team.

review_candidates.title: Senior Officer, Community Resilience

review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world's largest humanitarian network, comprised of 191 member National Societies. Addressing climate and environmental crises is the first strategic priority of the IFRC's Strategy 2030, which stresses the urgent need to massively scale up climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction in view of increasing disasters and their impacts on the most vulnerable populations. Against this backdrop, the Alliance for the Amazon (2025–2035) was established — a 10-year regional platform led by the IFRC and eight National Red Cross Societies (representing nine countries), formally launched at COP16 (Cali, October–November 2024). The Alliance seeks to address the humanitarian impacts of environmental and climate crises in the Amazon through a holistic approach grounded in three pillars: (i) disaster risk management and anticipatory action; (ii) integral health and community well-being; and (iii) resilient and sustainable livelihoods. A central element of its methodology is the recognition of indigenous and local knowledge systems as the foundation for the design of territorial resilience solutions, as expressed through the Dialogues of Knowledge Systems held in Colombia and Bolivia in 2025 and in Ecuador in 2026. The "Alliance for the Amazon – Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project” (22 months, EUR 500,000), funded by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), is the primary financial framework for this position in its initial phase. It operates across three active country nodes: Colombia (Colombian Red Cross, Leticia-Amazonas), Bolivia (Bolivian Red Cross, Guayaramerín-Beni) and Ecuador (Ecuadorian Red Cross, Alliance Regional Presidency). The IFRC ARO Secretariat serves as regional coordinator. Interventions prioritize the Disaster Risk Management and Anticipatory Action Pillar, combining participatory community assessments (EVCA), community early warning systems (EWS) and feasibility studies for Early Action Protocols (EAP), in dialogue with indigenous peoples, local authorities, national disaster risk management institutions and other sectoral institutions, and seeking opportunities to promote adaptation initiatives, including nature-based solutions that are critical for mid-term Amazon resilience. The Resilience Senior Officer will serve as Project Coordinator for the Alliance from the IFRC ARO Secretariat, acting as the operational and technical link between implementing National Societies, strategic partners and IFRC's programmatic structure. While the immediate focus is the implementation of the Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project, the role is conceived as part of the Alliance's long-term institutional structure, with the possibility of extension subject to the availability of additional funding. Job Duties And Responsibilities 2.1 Coordinate the Alliance for the Amazon and ensure quality, effective programming Serve as Project Coordinator for the Alliance from the IFRC ARO Secretariat, acting as the central point of coordination between implementing National Societies (CRC, CRB, CRE), the Andean CCD and the regional CER team. Support the coordinated implementation of the Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project across the Colombia, Bolivia and Ecuador nodes, ensuring methodological coherence, linkage between results and compliance with donor requirements. Provide technical advice to IFRC delegations and National Society teams on the integration of community-based disaster risk management, early warning systems (EWS) and anticipatory action approaches into country operational plans. Promote integrated approaches linking risk information, early warning, anticipatory action, livelihoods and ecosystem resilience, including nature-based approaches where relevant, with locally appropriate risk reduction measures. Support the design and implementation of participatory and intercultural community engagement methodologies (EVCA, participatory diagnostics, engagement with Indigenous Peoples as rights holders and knowledge holders), ensuring cultural relevance and community legitimacy across all three intervention nodes. Support rights-based, culturally appropriate and inclusive engagement with Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including respect for Indigenous governance systems, free, prior and informed consent where applicable, appropriate protocols for the use, protection and sharing of traditional and local knowledge, and mechanisms to ensure that communities influence decisions affecting their territories. Integrate protection, gender and inclusion considerations into programme design, community engagement, risk assessment, anticipatory action and monitoring, with particular attention to groups facing differentiated exposure, vulnerability or barriers to participation. Support resource mobilization and proposal development related to the Alliance and resilience in the Amazonian context, in coordination with IFRC ARO colleagues and National Societies. Support the identification and documentation of future resource-mobilization opportunities for the Alliance, including maintaining a funding and partnership pipeline and contributing to concept notes or other materials that can support future phases of the Alliance. Contribute, where appropriate, to the development of frameworks, tools, processes and knowledge products that can support the continued development and scaling of the Alliance beyond the current funding period, subject to future resources and strategic decisions. 2.2 Advance the position of the IFRC and the Alliance for the Amazon regionally and globally Support the positioning efforts of the Alliance Secretariat in strategic regional and global forums related to climate change, disaster risk management, anticipatory action and the resilience of Amazonian communities. Collect, systematize and document project progress, good practices and lessons learned to inform IFRC ARO's representation in key advocacy spaces — including lessons learned from the Global Anticipatory Action Dialogue, the Regional Disaster Risk Reduction Platform (March 2027) and the Regional Anticipatory Action Dialogue for the Americas (2027). Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued) Establish and facilitate practical mechanisms for systematic learning, reflection and adaptive management across Alliance countries, ensuring that evidence and experience from Alliance for the Amazon related projects such as the Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project implementation inform programme design, technical approaches, partnership decisions and future Alliance programming and resource mobilization. Produce high-quality institutional documents on Alliance programming — including technical reports, position notes, case studies and policy papers — for use across multiple platforms and audiences. Contribute to the development of Alliance communication and advocacy products, ensuring that community perspectives and territorial resilience approaches are the foundations of these products. Contribute to IFRC efforts in other departments as relevant (Policy, Partnerships, Communications, EW4All). 2.3 Coordinate with strategic partners and support inter-institutional articulation Coordinate with strategic partners of the Alliance for the Amazon, including The Nature Conservancy (TNC), to support areas of complementary expertise relevant to the Alliance, including the regional Early Action Protocol (EAP) roadmap, nature-based solutions, ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, community resilience, knowledge and learning, and resource mobilization, systematizing progress and informing Secretariat decision-making processes. Articulate the Alliance's work with other relevant regional and global initiatives — including EW4All, the Sendai Framework, National Disaster Risk Management Platforms and other relevant efforts implemented in the Amazon by other sectoral institutions — identifying synergies and positioning opportunities. Facilitate strategic collaboration between Alliance National Societies and partners with complementary technical, scientific, financing and implementation capabilities, ensuring that partnerships contribute to Alliance priorities and are aligned with National Society ownership. Facilitate linkages between country teams and the national authorities and institutions operating in the intervention areas (SINAGER-Bolivia, UNGRD-Colombia, SENAMHI and equivalents), supporting the project's articulation with national institutional frameworks. Support communication and dialogue between IFRC ARO and reference centres (IFRC Climate Centre, CREPD, CRECC), building bridges between their capacities and the Alliance's programmatic needs. Organize and facilitate peer coordination and South–South cooperation spaces between National Society technical staff, promoting the exchange of experiences in community resilience and anticipatory action in the Amazonian context. 2.4 Plan, monitor and report on the SPANISH COOPERATION (AECID) PROJECT Contribute to programmatic management and monitoring of Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project activities at the regional level, ensuring delivery of results on time, within budget and to agreed quality standards. 2.5 Contribute to an effective, high quality Alliance for the Amazon team Support National Society teams across the Alliance, both in-person and remotely, to achieve common objectives, including field missions to Spanish Cooperation (AECID) Project intervention nodes (Leticia-Colombia, Guayaramerín-Bolivia, Ecuador) and other Alliance spaces as needed. 2.6 Support Alliance governance coordination Support the coordination of Alliance governance, including preparation of strategic coordination meetings, decision records, action tracking, escalation of risks and issues. Education University degree in Anthropology, Social Sciences, Human Geography, Ethnology, Disaster Risk Management or related fields (Required) Post-graduate degree in disaster risk management, climate change, community resilience, sustainable development or related fields (Preferred) Technical training in community and indigenous peoples engagement methodologies, applied ethnography or intercultural participation (Required) Training in anticipatory action, disaster risk management or emergency preparedness — or demonstrable equivalent practical experience. review_candidates.description: Are you ready to take the lead on technically complex projects that build stronger, more resilient communities ? As a Project Director - Power, you will be at the forefront of driving success, managing a single project contract to ensure seamless execution from start to finish. With your expertise, you will oversee the budget, coordinate project personnel, and maintain a production schedule that guarantees timely delivery and exceptional quality. Collaborate with industry experts and committed teams to align project goals with o wner expectations, adhering to contract specifications and upholding the highest standards. Apply now and transform your career with us. What You Will Be Doing Manages all aspects of the project, including construction, budget and cash management for a single assigned project to ensure compliance with the project contract and owner needs. Produces the project schedule, pay estimates, project procedures, and equipment resources needed to complete accurate and timely project production. Works with external managing partnerships and Joint Ventures (JVs) to develop one unified project plan, if applicable. Develops and manages the project organizational chart and Company and/or JV supporting staff assignments for each phase of production, ensuring the accurate and timely completion of project objectives. Provides technical insight to project pursuits and participates in bid interviews, as necessary. Assesses the initial project contract and works with the owner to resolve specification, contract conflicts, and scheduling issues. Engages with all project stakeholders proactively, including managing partners, joint venture Executive Board, federal authorities such as Senators, Mayors, or Commissioners, local landowners, business owners, and regulatory bodies that will have influence over project success. Coordinates with the construction management team to identify project risks and negotiate change orders with the owner to ensure efficient and effective project production. Oversees project and construction management to accurately update the project construction schedule and adjust for any change orders from the Owner. Presents monthly project reports to Executive Leadership. Supports and promotes project safety by ensuring compliance with the project safety program, safety procedures, and owner safety policies. Reviews weekly safety reports and participates in monthly safety review meetings with project personnel. Directs construction management decisions regarding staff and equipment needs, ensuring cost containment with subcontractors and equipment billing. Resolves disputes with the project owner in a timely and compliant manner. Engages Company legal counsel and Executive leadership, where necessary. Provides input on equipment procurement methods and contracts to ensure efficient and effective project production. Leads project closeout procedures, finalizing contract paperwork, obtaining retainages, and working with management to resolve any project claims. Leads project debrief cycles to review all aspects of project work and completion. What We Are Looking For 15+ years’ experience in construction project management required. 10+ years’ experience in managing personnel required. Experience with heavy transmission on a project 230kV or higher required. Experience on 500/765 kV transmission highly preferred. Proven experience in bid-build, CMCG, design build and other alternative delivery projects required. Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or related field a plus. Valid Driver’s License Strong interpersonal skills proven to engage and retain positive working relationships. Strong proven skill to identify, track and manage project risk. Proven ability to efficiently and effectively manage multiple departments and direct reports to retain focus on one project completion goal and timeline. Proven ability to identify growth opportunities for project personnel and developed to coach and mentor project personnel. Proven ability to delegate task driven responsibilities to project personnel. Proven knowledge and ability to analyze and interpret financial documentation to identify and mitigate project risk. Effective delegation skills to drive efficient, accurate and profitable project completion. Strong internal branding and sales knowledge to constantly promote yourself and the Company brand. Why work for us Some of the benefits you may be eligible for as an employee are: Comprehensive compensation package and paid time off program Industry leading 401(k)/RRSP Medical/Extended Health Care, Dental, Vision and/or Provincial Medical Wellness benefits & Employee Assistance Program Tuition Reimbursement Program We are an EEO/ADA/Veterans employer. Salary Min USD $250,000.00/Yr. Salary Max USD $320,000.00/Yr.
